acceptance.criterion: `/omp <instructions>` on Claude Code and `$elves omp <instructions>` or equivalent natural language on Codex/Grok resolve `run_omp.sh` from the active installed Elves skill root.
The command is always `omp`; `opm` is neither accepted nor documented.
The shortcut uses a policy-admitted disposable snapshot, a finite hard wall limit, closed stdin, and a run-scoped profile.
Read-only behavior is the default. Any write form requires independent user implementation authority and the existing qualified writable-snapshot boundary.
No host `HOME`, agent configuration, Git credentials, PR authority, or merge authority is inherited.
Missing executable or auth, malformed NDJSON, timeout, incomplete terminal output, and cleanup failure return clear nonzero failures without affecting native routes.
An unmarked user-owned Claude alias is reported as a conflict before any installed skill files are changed.
`omp-cli` is a canonical built-in adapter with persistent-session and isolated-write capabilities; it never silently degrades to `custom-cli`.
Its canonical contract pair is `("none", "omp-jsonl")`: the complete packet is passed as a positional argv token after `--print`, not misrepresented as a prompt file or stdin transport.
`omp-jsonl` is a supported output contract with one strict decoder selected by `default_decoder_for_adapter`.
Create argv contains `--mode json`, exact worktree `--cwd`, requested model, thinking level, approval mode, isolated `--profile`, `--print`, and the complete redacted packet.
Resume argv contains `--resume <exact-uuid>` and never contains `--continue`, `-c`, bare `--resume`, latest/current selectors, or OMP `--prewalk`.
Profile `extra_args` cannot override `--mode`, `--cwd`, `--model`, `--thinking`, `--approval-mode`, `--profile`, `--print`, `--resume`, or session-selection controls.
The decoder binds session identity, model, usage, messages, and terminal state only from documented typed events.

Empty output, malformed rows, malformed or conflicting UUIDs, conflicting model evidence, invalid usage, missing output, missing terminal state, and size-limit violations fail with stable validation codes.
Existing Claude, Grok, Codex, Gemini, Antigravity, OpenCode, Devin, custom, and host-native registry and argv tests remain unchanged.

`full-run-prepare --adapter omp-cli` validates the staged packet, acceptance mapping, worktree, branch, protected refs, executable, requested model, thinking level, approval mode, and run profile before launch.
`full-run-launch`, `monitor`, `await`, `logs`, `stop`, and `reconcile` return the existing provider-neutral result shapes.
Create starts without a provider session ID. The first authoritative `session` event supplies the canonical UUID, which is persisted as `provider_session_id` before resume is permitted.
No listing, “current,” latest-session, or report-text fallback is used when the session event is missing.
Repeated identical session events are idempotent; zero session identities or conflicting identities block the run.

Resume requires the captured UUID, same worktree, same run profile, an authenticated prior host interruption, a closed prior process identity, unchanged packet/acceptance bindings, and a nonterminal event log.
Resume argv is inspected before spawn and must contain the exact `--resume <provider_session_id>` pair.
EOF or process exit zero without `agent_end` is incomplete rather than successful.
Nonzero exit, malformed terminal data, session/model conflict, unsafe branch movement, protected-ref movement, or missing identity produces a bounded blocked/interrupted result.
A healthy run may make meaningful commits on the assigned feature branch and wakes the parked driver only on terminal, safety, checkpoint, blocker, or explicit-stop conditions.
Reconciliation derives transport/session/model/usage evidence from the host decoder rather than worker report prose; worker `merge_authority` remains false.
Existing Grok and Devin full-run fixtures remain green without semantic changes.
Doctor/setup/onboard separately report executable presence, version, authentication, exact-resume support, NDJSON support, isolated-write support, usage reporting, and qualification.
Inventory never invents remaining quota, authentication success, model availability, or qualification.
Provider authentication is granted only through the exact selected and allowlisted environment variable or a separately qualified exact source projection.
Credentials for unselected providers are absent even if present in the host environment.
Every launch receives a private run HOME/XDG tree and a run-scoped `--profile`; the same profile identity is retained across exact resume.
Host `~/.claude/tools` is never copied, mounted wholesale, or exposed writable. A tool-name collision fails before launch or is handled using a run-owned exact tool installation.
Other agent configuration roots, SSH material, private keys, global Git configuration, and credential stores remain unavailable.
OMP provider auth does not imply GitHub push auth. Push remains a separate explicit host grant.
Explicit `omp-cli` selection may proceed only when capability and authority checks pass; otherwise routing records an honest native fallback.
Existing Grok consent, Devin behavior, and host-native route selection remain unchanged.
Documentation presents OMP as an optional trusted worker and retains Claude Code, Codex, and Grok Build as the supported main drivers.
Documentation explicitly distinguishes OMP `--prewalk` from Elves exact-session prewalk.
Create, session capture, follow, interruption, exact resume, profile isolation, auth grants, and host reconciliation have copy-paste examples.
The existing recursive `cobbler_runtime` shipment includes all new runtime code without introducing a new per-module copy list.
Existing Claude, Codex, and Grok skill roots receive the OMP worker runtime and reference; Phase 1 does not invent an OMP main-driver install root.
Installed-bundle smoke proves `omp-cli` retains its registry identity and that native operation does not require an installed `omp`.
If B0 is included, Claude’s managed alias inventory changes atomically from eleven to twelve while Codex and Grok continue to receive no Claude aliases.
Repository consistency checks reject `opm` when used as an Oh My Pi executable, adapter, profile, alias, or command.
Focused tests and the applicable repository verifier pass without weakening or skipping tests.
Qualification proves create, stream-derived UUID capture, exact resume, same worktree, same isolated profile, one logical stream, retained guide context, and route change.
The host-profile row defines identity events, provider-secret allowlist, worktree binding, usage source, commit mode, executable probes, and launch readiness.
`required` prewalk fails before the task launch when evidence is absent, malformed, version-mismatched, or stale.
`experimental` retains exact-session, worktree, packet, profile, process, and authority checks.
OMP `--prewalk` never appears in Elves prewalk argv or documentation.
Compaction de-qualification and post-edit cold-fallback rules remain identical across transports.
A separate policy decision explicitly adds OMP to the supported-main-driver list.
The official OMP skill discovery/install path is behaviorally verified; no `~/.omp/skills` or equivalent path is guessed.
A new installation target is added only after marker policy, first-install behavior, updates, conflicts, and cleanup are specified and tested.
Host parity covers invocation, helper resolution, canonical memory, stop control, prewalk, review, readiness, and landing authority.
OMP remains unable to grant itself merge, release, posting, secret, or protected-ref authority.
Claude, Codex, and Grok installation and alias behavior remain unchanged.

master_acceptance.criterion: A supported Elves host can stage one acceptance-bound packet and run OMP as an optional trusted parked implementation worker.
The host captures one exact OMP UUID from typed NDJSON and uses only `--resume <uuid>` for recovery.
Successful completion requires `agent_end`, process exit zero, valid identity/model evidence, and clean host safety checks.
Provider credentials, OMP profile state, worktree authority, GitHub push authority, and merge authority remain separate.
Missing OMP capability falls back honestly to native work and never makes OMP mandatory.
Existing Grok, Devin, and host-native behavior remains green.
User-facing documentation and installed bundles describe the supported Phase 1 route without implying Phase 2 or Phase 3 support.
